verses.1:1: To the brethren, the Jews throughout Egypt, the brethren, the Jews in Jerusalem and those in the country of Judea, send greetings and good peace.
verses.1:2: And may God do good to you, and remember His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, His faithful servants.
verses.1:3: And may He give to all of you a heart to worship Him and to do His will with a great heart and a willing soul.
verses.1:4: And may He open your heart in His law and in His statutes, and make peace.
verses.1:5: And may He hear your supplications, and be reconciled to you, and not forsake you in an evil time.
verses.1:6: And now we are here praying for you.
verses.1:7: In the reign of Demetrius, in the one hundred and sixty-ninth year, we the Jews wrote to you in the tribulation and in the extremity that came upon us in these years, from the time that Jason and those with him revolted from the holy land and the kingdom,
verses.1:8: and burned the gate, and shed innocent blood. Then we pleaded with the Lord and were heard; we offered sacrifice and fine flour, and brought forth the lamps, and set out the loaves.
verses.1:9: And now see that you keep the days of the Feast of Tabernacles of the month of Chislev.
verses.1:10: In the eighty-eighth year, in Jerusalem. And those in Judea, and the council of elders, and Judas, to Aristobulus, teacher of King Ptolemy, who is of the lineage of the anointed priests, and to the Jews in Egypt: greeting and good health.
verses.1:11: Having been saved by God out of great perils, we give great thanks to Him, as those who stood arrayed in battle against a king.
verses.1:12: For He Himself drove out into Persia those who were arrayed in battle in the holy city.
verses.1:13: For when the leader arrived with the force around him that seemed irresistible, they were cut to pieces in the temple of Nanea, through deceit employed by the priests of Nanea.
verses.1:14: For as though to marry her, Antiochus and the friends with him came to the place, in order to take the great treasures by way of a dowry.
verses.1:15: And when the priests of the temple of Nanea had set them forth, and he had entered with a few men into the enclosure of the sanctuary, they closed the temple as soon as Antiochus came in,
verses.1:16: and opening the secret door in the ceiling, they hurled stones and struck down the leader as with thunderbolts; and cutting them to pieces, they threw the heads out to those outside.
verses.1:17: Blessed in all things be our God, who gave over those who acted impiously.
verses.1:18: Since we are about to celebrate the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth day of Chislev, we have thought it necessary to inform you, so that you yourselves also may keep the Feast of Tabernacles and of the fire, as when Nehemiah, who built the temple and the altar at that time, offered sacrifices.
verses.1:19: For indeed, when our fathers were being led away into Persia, the devout priests secretly took some of the fire of the altar and hid it in the hollow of a waterless pit resembling a cistern, where they made it secure, so that the place was unknown to all.
verses.1:20: Now after many years had passed, when it pleased God, Nehemiah, having been sent by the king of Persia, sent the descendants of the priests who had hidden it for the fire.
verses.1:21: When they reported to us that they had not found fire, but thick water, he commanded them to draw it up and bring it. And when the things pertaining to the sacrifices were brought up, Nehemiah commanded the priests to sprinkle with the water both the wood and what was laid upon it.
verses.1:22: And when this was done and some time had passed, and the sun, which was overcast, shone forth, a great fire blazed up, so that all marveled.
verses.1:23: And the priests offered prayer while the sacrifice was being consumed—both the priests and all—with Jonathan leading and the rest responding, as did Nehemiah.
verses.1:24: And the prayer was in this manner: "O Lord God, Creator of all things, awesome and strong and righteous and merciful, the only King and gracious One,
verses.1:25: the only Provider, the only righteous and Almighty and eternal One, who delivers Israel from every evil, who made the fathers chosen and sanctified them:
verses.1:26: accept the sacrifice on behalf of all Your people Israel, and guard Your portion and consecrate it.
verses.1:27: Gather together our dispersion, set free those who are in bondage among the nations, look upon the despised and abhorred, and let the nations know that You are our God.
verses.1:28: Torment those who oppress and deal insolently in arrogance;
verses.1:29: plant Your people in Your holy place, just as Moses said."
verses.1:30: Then the priests sang the hymns.
verses.1:31: And when the things of the sacrifice were consumed, Nehemiah commanded that the remaining water also be poured over large stones.
verses.1:32: And when this was done, a flame was kindled; but when the light shone back from the altar, it was consumed.
verses.1:33: Now when the matter became known, and it was reported to the king of the Persians that in the place where the priests who had been carried away had hidden the fire, the water had appeared, with which Nehemiah and those with him also purified the sacrifices,
verses.1:34: the king, having examined the matter, enclosed the place and made it sacred;
verses.1:35: and from these things the king received many revenues, and also gave a share of them.
verses.1:36: Now Nehemiah and those with him called this Nephthar, which is interpreted "Purification"; but by most people it is called Nephthar.
verses.2:1: Now it is found in the records that Jeremiah the prophet commanded those who were being carried away to take some of the fire, as has been noted;
verses.2:2: and how the prophet charged those who were being carried away, having given them the law, that they should not forget the statutes of the Lord, nor be led astray in their minds upon seeing images of gold and silver and the adornment around them.
verses.2:3: And speaking other such words, he exhorted them that the law should not depart from their heart.
verses.2:4: It was also in the writing that the prophet, having received a divine revelation, commanded that the tabernacle and the ark should go with him, and how he went forth to the mountain where Moses went up and beheld the inheritance of God.
verses.2:5: And when Jeremiah came there, he found a cavernous chamber, and he brought the tabernacle and the ark and the altar of incense into it, and blocked up the entrance.
verses.2:6: And some of those who followed with him came to mark the way, but they could not find it.
verses.2:7: When Jeremiah learned of this, he rebuked them and said, "Indeed, the place shall be unknown until God gathers the congregation of the people together and mercy comes.
verses.2:8: And then the Lord will disclose these things, and the glory of the Lord and the cloud shall appear, as it was shown in the time of Moses, and as Solomon also prayed that the place might be greatly consecrated."
verses.2:9: It was also declared how he, possessing wisdom, offered the sacrifice of dedication and of the completion of the temple.
verses.2:10: Just as Moses prayed to the Lord, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the things of the sacrifice, so Solomon prayed to the Lord, and the fire came down and consumed the burnt offerings.
verses.2:11: And Moses said, "Because the sin offering was not eaten, it was consumed."
verses.2:12: In like manner Solomon also kept the eight days.
verses.2:13: The same things were also recounted in the records and in the memoirs concerning Nehemiah, and how, founding a library, he gathered together the books about the kings and prophets, and the writings of David, and letters of kings concerning votive offerings.
verses.2:14: In like manner Judas also gathered together these things that had been scattered on account of the war that happened to us, and they are with us.
verses.2:15: Therefore, if you have need of any of them, send those who will carry them to you.
verses.2:16: Since, therefore, we are about to celebrate the purification, we have written to you; you will therefore do well to keep the days.
verses.2:17: Now it is God who has saved all His people, and has restored His inheritance to all, and the kingdom, and the priesthood, and the sanctification,
verses.2:18: just as He promised through the law. For we have hope in God that He will swiftly have mercy upon us, and will gather us together from under heaven into the holy place; for He has delivered us out of great evils, and has purified the place.
verses.2:19: Now the things concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and the purification of the greatest temple, and the dedication of the altar,
verses.2:20: and further the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,
verses.2:21: and the manifestations that came from heaven to those who strove bravely with honor for Judaism, so that, though few in number, they plundered the whole country and pursued the barbarian multitudes,
verses.2:22: and recovered the temple renowned throughout the whole inhabited world, and liberated the city, and restored the laws that were about to be abolished, while the Lord with all forbearance became gracious to them—
verses.2:23: all these things, which have been set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five books, we shall attempt to abridge into a single volume.
verses.2:24: For considering the flood of figures and the difficulty that exists for those who wish to immerse themselves in the narratives of the history because of the abundance of the material,
verses.2:25: we have taken care to provide delight for those who wish to read, ease for those who are eager to commit it to memory, and profit for all who come to it.
verses.2:26: And for us who have undertaken the toil of this abridgment, the task is no easy thing, but a matter of sweat and sleeplessness,
verses.2:27: just as it is no light thing for one who prepares a banquet and seeks the benefit of others; nevertheless, for the sake of the gratitude of the many, we shall gladly endure the toil,
verses.2:28: leaving to the author the exact investigation of every detail, while ourselves lacking strength to follow the outlines of the abridgment.
verses.2:29: For just as the master builder of a new house must be concerned with the entire structure, while the one who undertakes to renovate and paint must consider what is suitable for its adornment, so, I think, it is with us also.
verses.2:30: To explore the ground, and to range widely in discourse, and to inquire closely into particulars belongs to the original author of the history;
verses.2:31: but to pursue brevity of expression and to forego an exhaustive treatment of the subject must be granted to the one who makes the summary.
verses.2:32: From here, then, let us begin the narrative, having added only this much to what has already been said; for it is foolish to enlarge what precedes the history while abridging the history itself.
verses.3:1: While the holy city was inhabited in all peace, and the laws were most excellently kept because of the godliness and hatred of wickedness of Onias the high priest,
verses.3:2: it came to pass that even the kings themselves honored the place and glorified the temple with the finest gifts;
verses.3:3: so that even Seleucus, the king of Asia, supplied out of his own revenues all the expenses belonging to the services of the sacrifices.
verses.3:4: Now a certain Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who had been appointed overseer of the temple, fell into a dispute with the high priest concerning the administration of the city market.
verses.3:5: And being unable to prevail against Onias, he went to Apollonius the son of Thrasaeus, who at that time was governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.
verses.3:6: And he reported that the treasury in Jerusalem was filled with untold riches, so that the abundance of the funds was beyond counting, and that they did not apply them to the account of the sacrifices, and that it was possible for these to come under the authority of the king.
verses.3:7: Now when Apollonius met with the king, he informed him concerning the riches that had been disclosed to him; and the king appointed Heliodorus, who was in charge of the affairs of state, and sent him with commands to carry out the removal of the aforementioned riches.
verses.3:8: Immediately Heliodorus set out on his journey, under the pretense of inspecting the cities throughout Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, but in reality to accomplish the purpose of the king.
verses.3:9: When he arrived in Jerusalem and had been courteously received by the high priest of the city, he recounted the report that had been made and declared plainly the reason for his presence; and he inquired whether these things were truly so.
verses.3:10: Then the high priest explained that these were deposits belonging to widows and orphans,
verses.3:11: and some also to Hyrcanus the son of Tobias, a man of very eminent standing—not as the impious Simon had falsely accused—and that the entire sum was four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold;
verses.3:12: and that to wrong those who had trusted in the holiness of the place, and in the majesty and inviolability of the temple honored throughout the entire world, was altogether impossible.
verses.3:13: But the other, because of the royal commands which he held, insisted that by all means these funds must be taken into the royal treasury.
verses.3:14: Having appointed a day, he went in to direct the inspection of these funds; and there was no small distress throughout the whole city.
verses.3:15: The priests cast themselves down before the altar in their priestly garments and called toward heaven upon Him who gave the law concerning deposits, to keep these things safe for those who had deposited them.
verses.3:16: Whoever beheld the appearance of the high priest was pierced in mind; for his countenance and the altered hue of his face revealed the agony within his soul.
verses.3:17: For a dread and shuddering of body had come over the man, through which the sorrow weighing upon his heart was made plain to those who watched.
verses.3:18: People rushed out from their houses in throngs to make public supplication, that the place might not be about to come into contempt.
verses.3:19: The women, girded with sackcloth beneath their breasts, thronged the streets; and of the maidens who were kept secluded, some ran together to the gates, others to the walls, and some looked out through the windows.
verses.3:20: And all of them, stretching out their hands toward heaven, offered up their prayer.
verses.3:21: It was pitiable to behold the mingled prostration of the multitude, and the anxious expectation of the high priest in his great agony.
verses.3:22: While they were calling upon the Almighty Lord to preserve the things entrusted wholly safe and secure for those who had entrusted them,
verses.3:23: Heliodorus proceeded to carry out what had been decreed.
verses.3:24: But when he had already arrived at the treasury with his guards, the Sovereign of spirits and of all authority brought about a great manifestation, so that all who had dared to accompany him were astounded at the power of God and fell into faintness and terror.
verses.3:25: For there appeared to them a horse with a fearsome rider, adorned with the finest trappings; and rushing fiercely forward, it struck at Heliodorus with its front hooves, while he who sat upon it appeared to be clad in full armor of gold.
verses.3:26: Moreover, two other young men appeared to him, remarkable in strength, most fair in speech, and splendid in apparel; and standing on either side of him, they scourged him unceasingly, inflicting many blows upon him.
verses.3:27: When he suddenly fell to the ground and was enveloped in thick darkness, they caught him up and placed him upon a litter;
verses.3:28: and this man, who just before had entered the aforementioned treasury with a great retinue and his entire bodyguard, they carried away rendered utterly helpless, having openly acknowledged the sovereign power.
verses.3:29: So he, by the divine working, lay speechless and bereft of all hope and deliverance;
verses.3:30: while they blessed the Lord who had wondrously glorified His own place; and the temple, which a little while before was full of fear and turmoil, now that the Almighty Lord had appeared, was filled with joy and gladness.
verses.3:31: Quickly some of the companions of Heliodorus begged Onias to call upon the Most High to grant life to him who lay altogether at his last breath.
verses.3:32: And the high priest, apprehensive lest the king should suppose that some foul deed had been committed against Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the man's recovery.
verses.3:33: While the high priest was making the atonement, the same young men appeared again to Heliodorus, arrayed in the same garments; and standing by him, they said, "Give great thanks to Onias the high priest, for on his account the Lord has granted you life.
verses.3:34: And you, having been scourged from heaven, proclaim to all the majestic power of God." And having spoken these words, they vanished from sight.
verses.3:35: Then Heliodorus offered a sacrifice to God and made very great vows to Him who had preserved his life; and having taken warm leave of Onias, he marched back with his forces to the king.
verses.3:36: And he bore open witness to all concerning the works of the supreme God which he had seen with his own eyes.
verses.3:37: When the king asked Heliodorus what sort of man would be fit to be sent once more to Jerusalem, he answered,
verses.3:38: "If you have any enemy or conspirator against the affairs of state, send him there, and you shall receive him back scourged, if indeed he even survives, because there is truly a certain power of God about that place.
verses.3:39: For He Himself who has His dwelling in heaven is the watcher and helper of that place, and He strikes and destroys those who come to do harm."
verses.3:40: And so the matters concerning Heliodorus and the preservation of the treasury came to pass.
verses.4:1: Now the aforementioned Simon, who had become an informer regarding the money and his homeland, spoke evil of Onias, claiming that he was the one who had incited Heliodorus and had been the contriver of the evils.
verses.4:2: And the benefactor of the city, the protector of his countrymen, and a zealot for the laws, he dared to call a conspirator against public affairs.
verses.4:3: As the enmity advanced to such a degree that murders were even committed by one of those approved by Simon,
verses.4:4: Onias, perceiving the peril of the contention, and seeing that Apollonius the son of Menestheus, the governor of Coele-Phoenicia and Syria, was increasing the malice of Simon,
verses.4:5: presented himself before the king, not becoming an accuser of his fellow citizens, but looking to what was beneficial both publicly and privately for the entire multitude.
verses.4:6: For he saw that without royal attention it was impossible for public affairs to obtain peace, and that Simon would not cease from his folly.
verses.4:7: Now when Seleucus departed this life, and Antiochus, who was called Epiphanes, received the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias corruptly usurped the high priesthood,
verses.4:8: promising the king in a petition three hundred and sixty talents of silver, and eighty talents from another source of revenue.
verses.4:9: In addition to these, he undertook to pay another one hundred and fifty talents, if it were granted to him by his authority to establish a gymnasium and a youth corps for himself, and to enroll those in Jerusalem as Antiochians.
verses.4:10: When the king consented and he gained control of the office, he immediately shifted his countrymen over to the Greek manner of life.
verses.4:11: And setting aside the royal privileges established for the Jews through John, the father of Eupolemus, who made the embassy for friendship and alliance with the Romans, and abolishing the lawful institutions, he introduced unlawful customs.
verses.4:12: For he gladly established a gymnasium directly beneath the citadel itself, and bringing the foremost of those in our time into subjection, he led them under the Greek hat.
verses.4:13: Now such was the height of Hellenism and the advance of foreign ways, because of the surpassing profanity of the ungodly Jason, who was no high priest,
verses.4:14: that the priests were no longer eager for the services of the altar; rather, despising the temple and neglecting the sacrifices, they hastened to partake of the unlawful provision in the wrestling arena after the summons of the discus,
verses.4:15: holding the ancestral honors as nothing, while regarding the Greek glories as the finest.
verses.4:16: For this very reason, a grievous calamity surrounded them; and the very ones whose ways of life they emulated, and whom they desired to resemble in every respect, they had as their enemies and avengers.
verses.4:17: For it is no light matter to act ungodly against the divine laws; yet the time that follows will declare these things.
verses.4:18: Now when the games held every fifth year were being celebrated in Tyre, and the king was present,
verses.4:19: the vile Jason sent envoys, as Antiochians from Jerusalem, carrying three hundred drachmas of silver for the sacrifice of Heracles; yet those who carried them requested that they not be used for sacrifice,
verses.4:20: but, on account of those who were present, for the construction of the triremes.
verses.4:21: Now when Apollonius the son of Menestheus was sent into Egypt for the enthronement ceremonies of King Philometor, Antiochus, learning that he was hostile to his own established affairs, took thought for his own security; therefore, having come to Joppa, he proceeded to Jerusalem.
verses.4:22: And being magnificently received by Jason and the city, he was welcomed in with torchlight processions and shouts; and after that, he marched his army into Phoenicia.
verses.4:23: Now after a period of three years, Jason sent Menelaus, the brother of the aforementioned Simon, to convey the money to the king and to complete memoranda concerning necessary matters.
verses.4:24: But he, having been presented to the king and having magnified him with the appearance of authority, diverted the high priesthood to himself, outbidding Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
verses.4:25: Having received the royal mandates, he arrived, bringing nothing worthy of the high priesthood, but possessing the fury of a cruel tyrant and the rage of a savage beast.
verses.4:26: So Jason, who had corruptly undermined his own brother, being himself undermined by another, was driven as a fugitive into the Ammonite country.
verses.4:27: Now Menelaus held fast to the office, yet of the money promised to the king he made no regular payment,
verses.4:28: although Sostratus, the commander of the citadel, demanded payment—for to him belonged the collection of the revenues. For this reason, the two of them were summoned by the king.
verses.4:29: And Menelaus left his own brother Lysimachus as deputy of the high priesthood, while Sostratus left Crates, who was over the Cyprians.
verses.4:30: While these matters were taking place, it came to pass that the people of Tarsus and Mallus revolted, because they were being given as a gift to Antiochis, the king's concubine.
verses.4:31: Therefore the king went in haste to settle affairs, leaving Andronicus, one of those held in high rank, as his deputy.
verses.4:32: Now Menelaus, supposing that he had found a favorable opportunity, stole certain golden vessels belonging to the temple and presented them to Andronicus, while others he had already sold to Tyre and the surrounding cities.
verses.4:33: And when Onias clearly learned of this, he reported it, having withdrawn to a place of sanctuary at Daphne, which lies near Antioch.
verses.4:34: Therefore Menelaus took Andronicus aside privately and urged him to do away with Onias; and Andronicus came to Onias, and having yielded to deceit and exchanged pledges with oaths, giving his right hand, even though he was regarded with suspicion, he persuaded him to come forth from the sanctuary, and immediately put him to death, having no reverence for justice.
verses.4:35: For this reason not only the Jews, but also many of the other nations, were indignant and deeply grieved at the unjust murder of the man.
verses.4:36: And when the king returned from the regions of Cilicia, the Jews in the city appealed to him, with the Greeks also sharing their hatred of the wickedness, because Onias had been slain without cause.
verses.4:37: Therefore Antiochus was grieved in his soul and moved to pity, and wept because of the self-control and great orderly conduct of the departed man;
verses.4:38: and inflamed with wrath, he immediately stripped off the purple robe of Andronicus and tore off his garments, and having led him around throughout the whole city to the very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, there he put the murderer out of the way, the Lord rendering to him the punishment he deserved.
verses.4:39: Now when many acts of sacrilege had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the report had spread abroad, the multitude gathered together against Lysimachus, for many golden vessels had already been carried away.
verses.4:40: And as the crowds were stirred up and filled with wrath, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men and began an unjust assault, led by a certain Auranus, a man advanced in years and no less advanced in ignorance.
verses.4:41: But perceiving the attack of Lysimachus, some snatched up stones, others thick pieces of wood, and some grabbed handfuls of the ashes lying nearby, and hurled them in confusion at those with Lysimachus.
verses.4:42: For this reason they wounded many of them, struck down some, and drove all of them into flight; and the temple robber himself they slew beside the treasury.
verses.4:43: Now concerning these matters, a trial was brought against Menelaus.
verses.4:44: And when the king arrived at Tyre, the three men sent by the council of elders presented their case before him.
verses.4:45: Now Menelaus, being already defeated, promised a considerable sum of money to Ptolemy the son of Dorymenes, to persuade the king.
verses.4:46: Therefore Ptolemy took the king aside into a colonnade, as if to refresh himself, and changed his mind.
verses.4:47: So he acquitted Menelaus, the cause of all the wickedness, of the charges brought against him; while those unfortunate men—who, even if they had pleaded before Scythians, would have been acquitted as blameless—he condemned to death.
verses.4:48: Swiftly, therefore, they suffered the unjust penalty—those who had spoken on behalf of the city, the peoples, and the sacred vessels.
verses.4:49: For this reason even the Tyrians, detesting the wickedness, magnificently provided what was needed for their burial.
verses.4:50: But Menelaus, through the covetousness of those in power, remained in office, growing in wickedness and standing forth as a great conspirator against his fellow citizens.
verses.5:1: Now about this time Antiochus undertook his second expedition into Egypt.
verses.5:2: And it came to pass throughout the whole city, for nearly forty days, that horsemen were seen charging through the air, wearing robes interwoven with gold and armed with lances in squadrons,
verses.5:3: and drawings of swords, and troops of cavalry drawn up in battle array, and assaults and charges taking place from both sides, and brandishings of shields, and multitudes of toils, and volleys of darts, and flashings of golden ornaments, and breastplates of every kind.
verses.5:4: Therefore all prayed that this apparition had occurred for good.
verses.5:5: Now when a false rumor arose that Antiochus had departed this life, Jason took no fewer than a thousand men and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and when those upon the wall were driven back and at last the city was already being captured, Menelaus fled into the citadel.
verses.5:6: And Jason carried out slaughters of his own citizens without mercy, not considering that good fortune against one's kinsmen is the greatest misfortune, but supposing that he was setting up trophies over enemies and not over his own countrymen.
verses.5:7: Yet he did not obtain the rule, but receiving shame as the outcome of his conspiracy, he departed once more as a fugitive into Ammanitis.
verses.5:8: At last, therefore, he met with an evil downfall: confined by Aretas the tyrant of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued by all, hated as a deserter of the laws, and abhorred as the executioner of his country and fellow citizens, he was cast out into Egypt.
verses.5:9: He who had banished many from their native land perished in a foreign land, having set sail to the Lacedaemonians as though to obtain shelter through their kinship;
verses.5:10: and he who had cast out a multitude unburied was himself unmourned, and had no share in any funeral rite or ancestral law.
verses.5:11: Now when word of what had happened reached the king, he concluded that Judea was in revolt; therefore, marching out from Egypt furious as a wild beast in his soul, he took the city by force of arms.
verses.5:12: And he commanded his soldiers to cut down without mercy those whom they encountered, and to slay those who went up into the houses.
verses.5:13: So there was a destruction of young and old, a wiping out of boys and women and children, and slaughters of virgins and infants.
verses.5:14: And eighty thousand perished in three days in all, forty thousand in violent hand-to-hand conflict, and no fewer than those who were slain were sold.
verses.5:15: Yet not content with these things, he dared to enter into the most holy temple of all the earth, having Menelaus as his guide, who had become a traitor both to the laws and to his country,
verses.5:16: and taking the sacred vessels with his polluted hands, and sweeping away with his profane hands the offerings dedicated by many kings for the advancement, glory, and honor of the place.
verses.5:17: And Antiochus was lifted up in his mind, not perceiving that because of the sins of those who dwelt in the city the Sovereign Lord was provoked to anger for a little while, and therefore disregard had come upon the place.
verses.5:18: Now if it had not come to pass that they were entangled in many sins, this man too, just like Heliodorus who was sent by King Seleucus to inspect the treasury, would immediately have been scourged as soon as he pressed forward and turned back from his presumption.
verses.5:19: Yet the Lord did not choose the nation for the sake of the place, but the place for the sake of the nation.
verses.5:20: Therefore the place itself also, having shared in the calamities that befell the nation, afterward partook of its blessings; and that which was forsaken in the wrath of the Almighty was restored again with all glory in the reconciliation of the great Sovereign Lord.
verses.5:21: So Antiochus carried off one thousand eight hundred talents from the temple and departed swiftly to Antioch, supposing in his arrogance that he could make the land navigable and the sea passable on foot, because of the loftiness of his heart.
verses.5:22: And he also left behind governors to afflict the race: in Jerusalem, Philip, a Phrygian by birth, and more barbarous in his character than the one who appointed him;
verses.5:23: and at Gerizim, Andronicus; and besides these, Menelaus, who exalted himself over his fellow citizens worse than all the others, having a hostile disposition toward the Jewish citizens.
verses.5:24: He also sent Apollonius, the commander of the Mysians, with an army of twenty-two thousand, commanding him to slay all who were of full age, and to sell the women and the younger ones.
verses.5:25: Now when he arrived in Jerusalem and feigned to be a man of peace, he held back until the holy day of the Sabbath; and finding the Jews resting from labor, he ordered those under him to turn out under arms.
verses.5:26: And he put to the sword all who had come out to watch the spectacle, and rushing into the city with his armed men, he subdued great multitudes.
verses.5:27: But Judas, who was also called Maccabeus, withdrew with about nine others, and lived in the mountains after the manner of wild beasts with those who were with him; and they continued feeding on wild herbs, so as not to partake of the defilement.
verses.6:1: Not long afterward, the king sent an Athenian elder to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers and no longer to live by the laws of God;
verses.6:2: and also to defile the temple in Jerusalem and call it the temple of Olympian Zeus, and to call the one at Gerizim—just as those who dwelt in the place were—the temple of Zeus the Friend of Strangers.
verses.6:3: Now the onset of this wickedness was harsh and altogether grievous to bear.
verses.6:4: For the temple was filled with debauchery and reveling by the Gentiles, who caroused with harlots and had intercourse with women within the sacred courts, and moreover brought inside things that were not lawful.
verses.6:5: And the altar was filled with abominable things forbidden by the laws.
verses.6:6: Neither was it possible to keep the Sabbath, nor to observe the feasts of their fathers, nor simply to confess oneself to be a Jew.
verses.6:7: And with bitter compulsion they drove them on the king's monthly birthday to partake of the sacrifices; and when the feast of Dionysus came, they were compelled to walk in procession for Dionysus wearing wreaths of ivy.
verses.6:8: Moreover, a decree went out to the neighboring Greek cities, at the suggestion of Ptolemy, that they should follow the same course against the Jews and make them partake of the sacrifices,
verses.6:9: and slay those who did not choose to adopt the Greek customs. Thus one might behold the distress that had come upon them.
verses.6:10: For two women were brought to trial for having circumcised their children; and hanging the infants from their breasts, and parading them publicly around the city, they cast them headlong down from the wall.
verses.6:11: And others, who had run together into the caves nearby to keep the seventh day secretly, were betrayed to Philip and were all burned together, because out of reverence they were unwilling to defend themselves, for the honor of that most solemn day.
verses.6:12: Now I urge those who read this book not to be discouraged because of these calamities, but to consider that these punishments were not for the destruction, but for the chastening of our race.
verses.6:13: For indeed, it is a token of great kindness when those who act ungodly are not left alone for a long time, but immediately fall under penalties.
verses.6:14: For not as with the other nations, where the Sovereign Lord waits patiently until they have come to the full measure of their sins before He punishes them, has He determined it to be with us;
verses.6:15: lest, when our sins have come to their full end, He should take vengeance upon us afterward.
verses.6:16: Therefore He never withdraws His mercy from us; and though He chastens with calamity, He does not forsake His own people.
verses.6:17: Yet let these things be spoken by us by way of reminder; and briefly we must proceed to the narrative.
verses.6:18: Eleazar, one of the foremost scribes, a man already advanced in years and most noble in the appearance of his countenance, was forced to open his mouth and eat swine's flesh.
verses.6:19: But he, welcoming death with honor rather than life with defilement, went forward of his own accord to the rack,
verses.6:20: having spat it out, coming forward in the manner in which those ought to come who are steadfast to reject what is not lawful to taste, even for the natural love of life.
verses.6:21: Now those who were appointed over that unlawful sacrificial feast, because of their acquaintance with the man from former times, took him aside privately and appealed to him to bring meat that was lawful for him to use, prepared by himself, and to pretend as though he were eating the meat from the sacrifice appointed by the king,
verses.6:22: so that by doing this he might be delivered from death, and on account of his longtime friendship with them might receive humane treatment.
verses.6:23: But he adopted a noble resolve, worthy of his years and of the dignity of his old age, and of his acquired and distinguished way of life, and of his most excellent conduct from childhood—and even more, in harmony with the holy and God-ordained law—and declared his mind accordingly, telling them to send him swiftly to Hades.
verses.6:24: "For it is not worthy of our age to pretend, lest many of the young, supposing that Eleazar at ninety years of age has gone over to an alien way of life,
verses.6:25: should themselves also be led astray through me because of my pretense and for the sake of a brief and momentary life, and so I should bring defilement and a stain upon my old age.
verses.6:26: For even if for the present time I should deliver myself from the punishment of men, yet neither living nor dead shall I escape the hands of the Almighty.
verses.6:27: Therefore, by manfully parting with this life now, I shall prove myself worthy of my old age,
verses.6:28: and leave behind to the young a noble example of how to die willingly and nobly for the revered and holy laws." And when he had spoken these words, he went immediately to the rack,
verses.6:29: while those who led him turned the goodwill they had shown toward him a little while before into ill will, because of the aforementioned words, which they themselves supposed to be madness.
verses.6:30: And when he was about to die under the blows, he groaned deeply and said, "To the Lord, who has the holy knowledge, it is manifest that, though I might have been delivered from death, I endure harsh pains in my body by being scourged, yet in my soul I gladly suffer these things out of fear of Him."
verses.6:31: So this man also departed this life in this manner, leaving his death as an example of nobility and a memorial of virtue, not only to the young, but also to the greater part of the nation.
verses.7:1: Now it also came to pass that seven brothers with their mother were seized and compelled by the king to partake of the unlawful swine's flesh, being tormented with whips and thongs.
verses.7:2: And one of them, becoming their spokesman, said, "Are you about to question and learn from us? For we are ready to die rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers."
verses.7:3: Then the king, becoming enraged, commanded pans and cauldrons to be heated red-hot.
verses.7:4: And when these were immediately heated, he commanded that the one who had become their spokesman have his tongue cut out, and that they scalp him and cut off his extremities, while the rest of his brothers and his mother looked on.
verses.7:5: And when he had become helpless in his remaining parts, he ordered him to be brought to the fire while still breathing and to be fried in the pan. And as the vapor from the pan spread far and wide, they exhorted one another, together with their mother, to die nobly, saying:
verses.7:6: "The Lord God looks on, and truly has compassion on us, just as Moses declared through the song that testifies against them to their face, saying, 'And He will have compassion on His servants.'"
verses.7:7: Now after the first had departed this life in this manner, they brought the second to the mockery; and tearing off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him, "Will you eat before your body is punished limb by limb?"
verses.7:8: But answering in the language of his fathers, he said, "No." Therefore also
verses.7:9: this one received the next torture in turn, just as the first. And when he was at his last breath, he said, "You indeed, accursed wretch, release us from this present life, but the King of the world will raise us up, who have died for His laws, to an everlasting renewal of life."
verses.7:10: And after him the third was mocked; and when his tongue was demanded, he quickly put it out and courageously stretched out his hands.
verses.7:11: And he nobly said, "From Heaven these have been called, and for the sake of His laws I disregard them, and from Him I hope to receive them back again."
verses.7:12: So the king himself and those with him were astonished at the spirit of the young man, because he counted the pains as nothing.
verses.7:13: And when this one also had departed this life, they tortured and tormented the fourth in the same manner.
verses.7:14: And when he was near death, he spoke thus: "It is preferable, when departing from men, to look for the hopes given by God to be raised up again by Him; for as for you, there shall be no resurrection to life."
verses.7:15: Next, bringing forward the fifth, they tormented him.
verses.7:16: But looking at him, he said, "Having authority among men, though you are perishable, you do what you wish; yet do not suppose that our race has been forsaken by God.
verses.7:17: But wait patiently, and behold His mighty power, how He will torment you and your seed."
verses.7:18: And after him they brought the sixth, and when he was about to die, he said, "Do not deceive yourself any further, for we suffer these things because of ourselves, having sinned against our own God; things worthy of wonder have come to pass;
verses.7:19: but do not think that you will go unpunished, having attempted to fight against God."
verses.7:20: Now the mother was exceedingly good and worthy of good remembrance, who, watching seven sons perish within the space of a single day, bore it with good courage because of her hopes in the Lord.
verses.7:21: And she exhorted each of the men in the language of their fathers, filled with a noble mind and arousing her womanly reasoning with manly courage, saying to them:
verses.7:22: "I do not know how you appeared in my womb, nor was it I who bestowed breath and life upon you, nor did I set in order the elements of each one of you.
verses.7:23: Therefore the Creator of the world, who formed the origin of man and devised the origin of all things, with mercy gives back to you both breath and life again, just as you now disregard yourselves for the sake of His laws."
verses.7:24: Now Antiochus, supposing that he was being despised and suspecting her reproachful voice, while the youngest was still alive, not only made his appeal with words, but also confirmed with oaths that he would at once make him rich and enviable if he turned away from the customs of his fathers, and would take him as a friend and entrust him with public affairs.
verses.7:25: But when the young man paid no attention at all, the king summoned the mother and urged her to become a counselor to the lad for his preservation.
verses.7:26: And after he had urged her at length, she agreed to persuade her son.
verses.7:27: Then leaning down toward him, deriding the cruel tyrant, she spoke thus in the language of their fathers: "Son, have mercy on me, who carried you in the womb nine months, and nursed you three years, and reared you and brought you to this age and sustained you.
verses.7:28: I implore you, child, to look up to the heaven and the earth, and seeing all that is in them, to know that God did not make them out of existing things, and in this way the race of mankind comes into being.
verses.7:29: Do not fear this executioner, but proving yourself worthy of your brothers, accept death, so that in mercy I may receive you back together with your brothers."
verses.7:30: While she was still finishing, the young man said, "What are you waiting for? I do not obey the command of the king, but I obey the command of the law that was given to our fathers through Moses.
verses.7:31: But you, who have become the deviser of every evil against the Hebrews, shall by no means escape the hands of God.
verses.7:32: For we are suffering because of our own sins;
verses.7:33: and if for the sake of rebuke and chastening our living Lord has been angry for a little while, He will also be reconciled again to His own servants.
verses.7:34: But you, O unholy man and most defiled of all men, do not be lifted up in vain, raging proudly with uncertain hopes, raising your hand against the heavenly children;
verses.7:35: for you have not yet escaped the judgment of the Almighty, all-seeing God.
verses.7:36: For our brothers, having now endured a brief pain, have fallen under God's covenant of everlasting life; but you, by the judgment of God, shall receive the just penalties of your arrogance.
verses.7:37: And I, like my brothers, give up both body and fortune for the laws of our fathers, as we call upon God speedily to become merciful to our nation, and that you, through torments and scourges, may confess that He alone is God;
verses.7:38: and in me and in my brothers to bring to an end the wrath of the Almighty, which has been justly kindled against our entire race."
verses.7:39: Then the king, becoming enraged, treated this one more cruelly than the others, feeling bitter over his derision.
verses.7:40: So this one also departed this life undefiled, trusting wholly in the Lord.
verses.7:41: And last of all, after her sons, the mother died.
verses.7:42: Let this much, then, suffice to have been declared concerning the sacrificial meats and the exceeding torments.
verses.8:1: Now Judas, who is also called Maccabeus, and those with him entered secretly into the villages and summoned their kinsmen; and gathering to themselves those who had remained in Judaism, they assembled about six thousand men.
verses.8:2: And they called upon the Lord to look upon the people who were oppressed by all, and also to have compassion on the temple that had been profaned by ungodly men;
verses.8:3: and to have mercy also on the city that was being destroyed and about to be leveled to the ground, and to hear the blood that cried out to Him;
verses.8:4: and also to remember the lawless destruction of the innocent infants, and the blasphemies committed against His name, and to show His hatred of evil.
verses.8:5: Now once Maccabeus had assembled an organized force, he became irresistible to the Gentiles, for the wrath of the Lord had turned to mercy.
verses.8:6: Coming unexpectedly upon cities and districts, he set them on fire; and seizing strategic places and routing not a few of the enemies,
verses.8:7: he especially chose the nights as allies for such assaults; and the report of his valor resounded everywhere.
verses.8:8: Now when Philip saw that the man was gaining ground little by little and advancing more frequently in his successes, he wrote to Ptolemy, the governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, to come to the aid of the king's affairs.
verses.8:9: And he promptly appointed Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of the chief Friends, and sent him out, placing under his command no fewer than twenty thousand Gentiles of all nations to wipe out the entire race of Judea; and with him they also appointed Gorgias, a general and a man well experienced in matters of war.
verses.8:10: Now Nicanor determined to make up for the king the tribute owed to the Romans, amounting to two thousand talents, from the enslavement of the Jews.
verses.8:11: Immediately he sent to the coastal cities, inviting them to purchase Jewish slaves, promising to deliver ninety slaves for a talent—not expecting the judgment from the Almighty that was about to overtake him.
verses.8:12: Word reached Judas concerning the advance of Nicanor; and when he informed those with him of the approach of the army,
verses.8:13: the cowardly and those who distrusted the justice of God fled and removed themselves from the region;
verses.8:14: while the others sold all that remained to them, and at the same time implored the Lord to deliver those who had been sold by the impious Nicanor before they had even met him;
verses.8:15: and if not for their own sake, yet for the sake of the covenants made with their fathers, and because His venerable and majestic name had been called upon them.
verses.8:16: Then Maccabeus gathered those who were with him, six thousand in number, and exhorted them not to be terrified by the captives nor to fear the vast multitude of the Gentiles who had come unjustly against them, but to contend nobly,
verses.8:17: keeping before their eyes the outrage lawlessly perpetrated by them against the holy place, and the cruel abuse of the mocked city, and moreover the overthrow of their ancestral way of life.
verses.8:18: "For they trust in weapons and in deeds of daring," he said, "but we trust in the Almighty God, who is able with a single nod to overtake both those who are coming against us and the whole world."
verses.8:19: Moreover, he recounted to them the acts of deliverance granted in the days of their forefathers, both that in the time of Sennacherib, when one hundred and eighty-five thousand perished,
verses.8:20: and the battle that took place in Babylonia against the Galatians, how all who came to the engagement were eight thousand together with four thousand Macedonians, and when the Macedonians were hard pressed, the six thousand destroyed the one hundred and twenty thousand because of the help that came to them from heaven, and they took great plunder.
verses.8:21: Having by these words made them courageous and ready to die for the laws and their country, he divided the army into four parts.
verses.8:22: He appointed his brothers as leaders of each division—Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan—placing one thousand five hundred men under each of them,
verses.8:23: and also Eleazar. Then, having read aloud the sacred book and given the watchword, "God's Help," he himself took the lead of the first division and engaged Nicanor in battle.
verses.8:24: And with the Almighty becoming their ally, they slew more than nine thousand of the enemies, wounded and maimed in their limbs the greater part of Nicanor's army, and forced them all to flee.
verses.8:25: They seized the money of those who had come to buy them; and after pursuing them for a considerable distance, they turned back from the region, being constrained;
verses.8:26: for it was the observance before the Sabbath, for which reason they did not prolong their pursuit of them.
verses.8:27: When they had collected their weapons and stripped the spoils from the enemies, they occupied themselves with the Sabbath, exceedingly blessing and giving thanks to the Lord who had preserved them to that day, having appointed for them a beginning of mercy.
verses.8:28: After the Sabbath, having distributed a portion of the spoils to those who had been tortured, and to the widows and the orphans, they divided the rest among themselves and their children.
verses.8:29: When they had done these things and offered a common supplication, they implored the merciful Lord to be wholly reconciled to His servants.
verses.8:30: And engaging in battle with the forces of Timothy and Bacchides, they slew more than twenty thousand of them, gained complete mastery of very high fortresses, and divided abundant plunder, making equal shares for themselves and for the tortured, the orphans, the widows, and also the aged.
verses.8:31: Having collected their weapons, they carefully stored all of them in strategic places, and brought the rest of the spoils to Jerusalem.
verses.8:32: They also slew the commander of Timothy's forces, a most wicked man who had inflicted many griefs upon the Jews.
verses.8:33: And while celebrating the victory in their homeland, they burned those who had set fire to the sacred gates, including Callisthenes, who had fled into a small house; and thus he received the fitting reward for his impiety.
verses.8:34: Now the thrice-accursed Nicanor, who had brought three thousand merchants for the sale of the Jews,
verses.8:35: having been humbled through the help of the Lord by those whom he considered to be the least of all, laid aside his glorious apparel and, making his way alone like a runaway slave through the inland country, arrived at Antioch, having prospered beyond all measure in the destruction of his army.
verses.8:36: And he who had undertaken to pay the tribute to the Romans from the captives of those in Jerusalem now proclaimed that the Jews had a Champion, and that for this reason the Jews were invulnerable, because they followed the laws ordained by Him.
verses.9:1: Now about that time, Antiochus happened to be retreating in disorder from the regions of Persia.
verses.9:2: For he had entered the city called Persepolis and attempted to rob the temples and to hold the city in subjection; therefore the multitudes rushed out and turned to the aid of arms, and it happened that Antiochus was put to flight by the inhabitants and made a disgraceful retreat.
verses.9:3: And while he was at Ecbatana, word reached him of what had happened to Nicanor and to the forces of Timothy.
verses.9:4: Carried away with fury, he thought to vent upon the Jews even the injury done by those who had put him to flight; therefore he commanded his charioteer to drive without ceasing and complete the journey, though the judgment from heaven was already accompanying him. For he had spoken thus arrogantly: "I will make Jerusalem a common burial ground of the Jews when I arrive there."
verses.9:5: But the all-seeing Lord, the God of Israel, struck him with an incurable and unseen blow; for no sooner had he ceased speaking than an irremediable pain in his bowels seized him, and bitter torments of his inward parts,
verses.9:6: most justly, since he had tortured the inward parts of others with many and strange afflictions.
verses.9:7: Yet he by no means ceased from his insolence, but was still filled with arrogance, breathing fire in his rage against the Jews and commanding the journey to be hastened. And it happened that he also fell from his chariot as it sped swiftly along, and suffering a grievous fall, every limb of his body was racked and wrenched.
verses.9:8: Thus he who in superhuman arrogance presumed to rival the waves of the sea, and supposed he could weigh the heights of the mountains in a balance, was brought down to the ground and carried in a litter, displaying to all the manifest power of God;
verses.9:9: so that worms even swarmed from the body of the impious man, and while he was still alive in agony and pain his flesh fell away, and by his stench the whole army was oppressed by his decay.
verses.9:10: And the man who a little while before thought he could touch the stars of heaven, no one could bear to carry because of the intolerable burden of the stench.
verses.9:11: There, then, broken as he was, he began to cease from the greatness of his arrogance and to come to his senses under the divine scourge, as his pains intensified every moment.
verses.9:12: And when he could no longer endure even his own stench, he said these words: "It is right to be subject to God, and for one who is mortal not to think arrogant thoughts."
verses.9:13: Then the wretch prayed to the Sovereign Lord, who would no longer have mercy on him, declaring thus:
verses.9:14: that he would proclaim free the holy city, which he had been hastening to level to the ground and establish as a common burial ground;
verses.9:15: and that the Jews, whom he had resolved not even to deem worthy of burial, but to destroy along with their infants as food for birds and wild beasts, he would make all of them equal to the Athenians;
verses.9:16: and that he would adorn with the finest votive offerings the holy temple which he had previously plundered, and restore all the sacred vessels many times over, and supply from his own revenues the expenses required for the sacrifices;
verses.9:17: and in addition to these things, that he would also become a Jew and go through every inhabited place proclaiming the mighty power of God.
verses.9:18: Yet when his sufferings by no means ceased, for the righteous judgment of God had come upon him, he despaired of his condition and wrote to the Jews the letter transcribed below, in the form of a supplication, containing these words:
verses.9:19: "To the worthy Jewish citizens, hearty greetings, good health, and prosperity, from Antiochus, King and General.
verses.9:20: May you be well, and your children; and your own affairs shall be according to your desire. Placing my hope in heaven,
verses.9:21: I remembered your honor and goodwill with deep affection. Having returned from the regions of Persia and fallen into a troublesome illness, I have judged it necessary to take thought for the common security of you all,
verses.9:22: not despairing of my own condition, but having great hope that I shall escape from this illness.
verses.9:23: Yet considering that my father also, at the times when he marched into the upper regions, appointed his successor,
verses.9:24: so that if anything unexpected should happen or anything grievous should come to pass, the people in the country, knowing to whom the affairs of state had been left, might not be thrown into confusion;
verses.9:25: and observing in addition that the neighboring rulers and those bordering the kingdom are watching for opportunities and awaiting what will happen, I have appointed my son Antiochus as king, whom I often entrusted and commended to most of you when I hurried up to the upper satrapies; and I have written to him what is set forth below.
verses.9:26: Therefore I urge and request you, remembering the benefits conferred both publicly and privately, that each of you preserve your present goodwill toward me and my son;
verses.9:27: for I am persuaded that he, being aligned with my purpose, will deal with you mildly and humanely."
verses.9:28: So the murderer and blasphemer, having suffered the worst torments, just as he had dealt with others, ended his life by a most pitiable death in a foreign land among the mountains.
verses.9:29: And Philip, his foster brother, escorted the body home; then, fearing the son of Antiochus, he crossed over into Egypt to Ptolemy Philometor.
verses.10:1: Now Maccabeus and those with him, as the Lord led them forward, recovered the temple and the city.
verses.10:2: And they tore down the altars constructed in the marketplace by the foreigners, and also the sacred precincts.
verses.10:3: Having cleansed the sanctuary, they made another altar; and striking stones and taking fire from them, they offered up sacrifices after a period of two years, together with incense and lamps, and made the setting forth of the loaves.
verses.10:4: When they had done these things, they implored the Lord, falling prostrate upon their bellies, that they might no longer fall into such evils, but that if they should ever sin, they might be dealt with by Him with gentleness and not be delivered over to blasphemous and barbarous nations.
verses.10:5: Now on the very day on which the sanctuary had been profaned by foreigners, it came to pass that on that same day the cleansing of the temple took place, on the twenty-fifth of the same month, which is Chislev.
verses.10:6: And with gladness they observed eight days in the manner of the Feast of Tabernacles, remembering how a little time before, during the Feast of Tabernacles, they had been roaming in the mountains and in the caves after the manner of wild beasts.
verses.10:7: Therefore, bearing leafy wands and beautiful branches, and also palm branches, they gave thanks to Him who had given them success in cleansing His own place.
verses.10:8: And they ordained by a common edict and decree for the whole nation of the Jews to observe the tenth days year by year.
verses.10:9: Now such were the events concerning the end of Antiochus, who was called Epiphanes.
verses.10:10: Now we will declare the events concerning the supreme Antiochus, who was the son of that ungodly man, summarizing the evils that afflicted the cities.
verses.10:11: For when he succeeded to the kingdom, he appointed a certain Lysias over the affairs of state, and as chief governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.
verses.10:12: For Ptolemy, who was called Macron, taking the lead in maintaining justice toward the Jews because of the wrong that had been done against them, endeavored to conduct affairs with them peacefully.
verses.10:13: Therefore, being accused by the Friends before Eupator and hearing himself called a traitor at every turn—because he had abandoned Cyprus, which had been entrusted to him by Philometor, and had gone over to Antiochus Epiphanes, and had not upheld his noble office in a noble manner—he poisoned himself and departed this life.
verses.10:14: Now Gorgias, upon becoming governor of those regions, maintained mercenary troops and at every turn kept up war against his own people.
verses.10:15: Together with these events, the Idumeans also, being in control of strategic strongholds, harassed the Jews, and taking in those who had fled from Jerusalem, they attempted to keep up the war.
verses.10:16: But those with Maccabeus, having offered solemn supplication and implored God to become their ally, rushed against the strongholds of the Idumeans.
verses.10:17: Assaulting these vigorously, they gained control of the positions, drove back all who were fighting upon the wall, and slaughtered those who fell into their hands, slaying no fewer than twenty thousand.
verses.10:18: Now when no fewer than nine thousand fled together into two exceedingly strong towers that had everything needed for a siege,
verses.10:19: Maccabeus himself departed for places of urgent need, leaving behind Simon and Joseph, and also Zacchaeus and those with him, in sufficient number to besiege them.
verses.10:20: But those with Simon, overcome by the love of money, were bribed with silver by some of those in the towers; and receiving seventy thousand drachmas, they allowed some of them to slip away.
verses.10:21: When they reported to Maccabeus concerning what had happened, he assembled the leaders of the people and brought an accusation that those men had sold their brethren for silver by releasing their enemies against them.
verses.10:22: So he put these men to death for becoming traitors, and immediately captured the two towers.
verses.10:23: And succeeding in everything with weapons in his hands, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in the two strongholds.
verses.10:24: Now Timothy, who had previously been defeated by the Jews, gathered together a vast multitude of foreign forces and assembled no small number of horses from Asia, and he came as though to take Judea captive by the spear.
verses.10:25: As he drew near, those with Maccabeus turned to supplication to God, sprinkling earth upon their heads and girding their loins with sackcloth,
verses.10:26: and falling down upon the step opposite the altar, they implored Him to be gracious to them, to be an enemy to their enemies and an adversary to their adversaries, just as the law also declares.
verses.10:27: When they had finished their prayer, they took up their weapons and advanced a considerable distance from the city; and when they drew near to the enemy, they kept to themselves.
verses.10:28: Just as the dawn was spreading abroad, both sides joined battle: the one having as a pledge of success and victory, along with valor, their refuge in the Lord, while the other appointed their fury as the leader of the conflict.
verses.10:29: When the battle grew fierce, there appeared to the adversaries out of heaven five resplendent men upon horses with golden bridles; and two of them, leading the Jews,
verses.10:30: took Maccabeus into their midst and, shielding him with their own full armor, kept him unharmed, while upon the enemies they hurled arrows and thunderbolts; therefore, confounded with blindness, they were cut to pieces, filled with panic.
verses.10:31: And twenty thousand five hundred were slaughtered, and six hundred horsemen.
verses.10:32: But Timothy himself fled for refuge into a stronghold called Gazara, a very strong fortress, where Chaereas was commander.
verses.10:33: And those with Maccabeus eagerly besieged the fortress for forty days.
verses.10:34: And those within, trusting in the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly and uttered profane words.
verses.10:35: Now as the twenty-fifth day was dawning, young men from among those with Maccabeus, inflamed in their anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall, and manfully and with savage fury cut down everyone who fell in their way.
verses.10:36: And others likewise climbed up during the diversion against those within, set fire to the towers, and kindling fires, burned the blasphemers alive; while others broke down the gates, and admitting the rest of the force, took possession of the city,
verses.10:37: and they slaughtered Timothy, who had hidden himself in a certain cistern, along with his brother Chaereas and Apollophanes.
verses.10:38: When they had accomplished these things, with hymns and thanksgiving they blessed the Lord, who bestows great benefits upon Israel and grants them the victory.
verses.11:1: Now after a very short space of time, Lysias, the guardian of the king, his kinsman, and the one set over the affairs of state, being exceedingly displeased at the things that had happened,
verses.11:2: gathered about eighty thousand men and all the cavalry, and came against the Jews, intending to make the city a dwelling place for Greeks,
verses.11:3: and to levy tribute upon the temple, as upon the rest of the sanctuaries of the nations, and to put the high priesthood up for sale every year;
verses.11:4: in no way taking into account the might of God, but elated in mind by his tens of thousands of foot soldiers, his thousands of horsemen, and his eighty elephants.
verses.11:5: So entering into Judea and drawing near to Beth-zur, which was a fortified place distant from Jerusalem by about five leagues, he pressed it hard.
verses.11:6: Now when Maccabeus and those with him learned that he was besieging the strongholds, they, together with the multitudes, implored the Lord with lamentations and tears to send a good angel for the salvation of Israel.
verses.11:7: And Maccabeus himself was the first to take up arms, and he urged the others to hazard their lives together with him to come to the aid of their brethren; and with one accord they rushed forth eagerly.
verses.11:8: And while they were right there near Jerusalem, a horseman in white apparel appeared leading them on, brandishing weapons of gold.
verses.11:9: Then all of them together blessed the merciful God, and were so strengthened in their souls that they were ready to pierce through not only men, but even the fiercest beasts and walls of iron.
verses.11:10: They advanced in battle array, having their ally from heaven, for the Lord had shown mercy to them.
verses.11:11: And hurling themselves like lions upon the enemies, they struck down eleven thousand of them and one thousand six hundred horsemen, and forced all the rest to flee.
verses.11:12: Most of them escaped wounded and unarmed; and Lysias himself escaped by shameful flight.
verses.11:13: Yet not being without understanding, he reflected within himself upon the defeat that had befallen him, and perceiving that the Hebrews were unconquerable because the mighty God fought on their side, he sent messengers to them
verses.11:14: and urged them to come to a settlement upon all just terms, promising that he would also persuade the king, constraining him to become their friend.
verses.11:15: And Maccabeus consented to everything that Lysias proposed, having regard for the common good; for whatever Maccabeus delivered to Lysias in writing concerning the Jews, the secretary granted.
verses.11:16: For the letter written to the Jews from Lysias was to this effect: "Lysias to the multitude of the Jews, greeting.
verses.11:17: John and Absalom, who were sent from you, having delivered the petition written below, made request concerning the matters indicated in it.
verses.11:18: Therefore, whatever needed to be brought before the king as well, I have clearly set forth to him, and what was admissible he has granted.
verses.11:19: If, then, you maintain your goodwill toward the government, for the future also I will endeavor to promote your good.
verses.11:20: Concerning the particulars of these matters, I have given instructions both to these men and to my own representatives to confer with you.
verses.11:21: Farewell. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the twenty-fourth day of Dioscorinthius."
verses.11:22: Now the king's letter ran as follows: "King Antiochus to his brother Lysias, greeting.
verses.11:23: Since our father has passed over to the gods, who desired that those of the kingdom should be undisturbed and attend to the care of the Jews,
verses.11:24: and we have heard that the Jews do not consent to our father's shift to Greek customs, but prefer their own way of life and request that their lawful observances be granted to them;
verses.11:25: desiring, therefore, that this nation also should be free from disturbance, we determine that the temple be restored to them, and that they conduct their lives according to the customs of their forefathers.
verses.11:26: You will do well, therefore, to send messengers to them and give them the right hand of friendship, so that, knowing our purpose, they may be of good cheer and gladly attend to the management of their own affairs."
verses.11:27: And to the nation the king's letter was as follows: "King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews and to the rest of the Jews, greeting.
verses.11:28: May you be well; it would be as we desire, and we ourselves also are in good health.
verses.11:29: Menelaus has made known to us his desire that you should return home and attend to your own affairs.
verses.11:30: Therefore, for those who return home up to the thirtieth day of Xanthicus, there shall be a pledge of friendship with full amnesty,
verses.11:31: so that the Jews may make use of their own provisions and laws, just as before; and none of them shall in any way be troubled concerning things done in ignorance.
verses.11:32: I have also sent Menelaus to encourage you.
verses.11:33: Farewell. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth day of Xanthicus."
verses.11:34: The Romans also sent a letter to them, reading as follows: "Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, envoys of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greeting.
verses.11:35: Concerning the things which Lysias, the kinsman of the king, has granted to you, we also give our consent.
verses.11:36: As for the matters which he decided should be referred to the king, consider them and send someone immediately, so that we may proceed as befits us; for we are on our way to Antioch.
verses.11:37: Therefore make haste and send some men, so that we also may know what your mind is.
verses.11:38: Be in good health. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth day of Xanthicus."
verses.12:1: Now when these agreements had been made, Lysias departed to the king, and the Jews occupied themselves with farming.
verses.12:2: But of the local commanders, Timothy and Apollonius the son of Gennaeus, and also Hieronymus and Demophon, and in addition to these Nicanor the commander of the Cypriots, would not allow them to remain settled and live in quietness.
verses.12:3: And the people of Joppa perpetrated so great an impiety: they invited the Jews who dwelt among them to embark with their wives and children into the boats they had provided, as though there were no ill will toward them;
verses.12:4: and in accordance with the common decree of the city, when these also accepted, as those who desired to live in peace and harbored no suspicion, they led them out and drowned them, not fewer than two hundred.
verses.12:5: Now when Judas heard of the cruelty that had been done to his countrymen, he gave orders to the men who were with him,
verses.12:6: and having called upon God, the righteous Judge, he came against the murderers of his brethren, set fire to the harbor by night, burned up the boats, and pierced through those who had fled there for refuge.
verses.12:7: And because the town was closed against him, he withdrew, intending to come back and root out the entire community of the people of Joppa.
verses.12:8: But when he learned that those in Jamnia also intended to act in the same manner toward the Jews who dwelt there,
verses.12:9: he fell upon the people of Jamnia also by night, and set fire to the harbor along with the fleet, so that the glare of the light was seen as far as Jerusalem, a distance of two hundred and forty stadia.
verses.12:10: When they had marched away nine stadia from there, making their advance against Timothy, Arabs fell upon him, not fewer than five thousand, with five hundred horsemen.
verses.12:11: And when a fierce battle took place, and those with Judas prospered through the help of God, the nomads, having been defeated, appealed to Judas to give them his right hand in pledge, promising both to give them cattle and to assist them in other ways.
verses.12:12: And Judas, supposing that they would truly be useful in many things, consented to make peace with them; and having received the pledge of his right hand, they departed to their tents.
verses.12:13: He also fell upon a certain city, laying a causeway against it—a strong city, enclosed with walls and inhabited by mixed nations, whose name was Caspin.
verses.12:14: And those within, trusting in the strength of their walls and in their store of provisions, behaved very insolently toward those with Judas, reviling them, and moreover blaspheming and speaking things that are not lawful.
verses.12:15: Then those with Judas, having called upon the great Sovereign of the world, who without battering rams or engines of war cast down Jericho in the days of Joshua, rushed fiercely against the wall.
verses.12:16: And having captured the city by the will of God, they carried out an unspeakable slaughter, so that the adjoining lake, which was two stadia wide, appeared to be filled with the blood that flowed into it.
verses.12:17: And having marched seven hundred and fifty stadia from there, they arrived at Charax, and to the Jews who are called Tubieni.
verses.12:18: Now they did not overtake Timothy in those regions, for he had departed from those parts without accomplishing anything, though he had left behind a very strong garrison in a certain place.
verses.12:19: But Dositheus and Sosipater, who were commanders under Maccabeus, marched out and destroyed those whom Timothy had left in the stronghold, more than ten thousand men.
verses.12:20: Then Maccabeus, having arranged the army with him in divisions, appointed them over the divisions; and they marched against Timothy, who had with him one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and two thousand horsemen and seven thousand besides.
verses.12:21: When Timothy heard of the approach of Judas, he sent the women and the rest of the baggage ahead to the place called Carnion; for the place was hard to besiege and difficult to approach because of the narrowness of all the passes.
verses.12:22: But when the division of Judas appeared first, terror fell upon the enemy, and fear came upon them from the manifestation of Him who beholds all things; they rushed into flight, each driven in a different direction, so that they were often wounded by their own men and pierced through by the points of their swords.
verses.12:23: And Judas pressed the pursuit all the more vigorously, piercing through those wicked men, and he destroyed about thirty thousand men.
verses.12:24: And Timothy himself, having fallen into the hands of those with Dositheus and Sosipater, appealed with much craftiness that they let him go safely, because he held the parents of many and the brothers of others, and it would come to pass that these would be shown no regard.
verses.12:25: So after he had confirmed with many words his agreement to restore them unharmed, they released him for the sake of saving their brethren.
verses.12:26: Then he marched out against Carnion and the temple of Atargatis, and slaughtered twenty-five thousand persons.
verses.12:27: And after the rout and destruction of these, he also marched against Ephron, a fortified city, in which there were multitudes of every tribe; and vigorous young men stationed before the walls fought stoutly, and there were great stores of engines of war and missiles.
verses.12:28: But having called upon the Sovereign who with might shatters the strength of the enemy, they took the city into their hands, and struck down about twenty-five thousand of those who were within.
verses.12:29: And departing from there, they hastened toward Scythopolis, which is six hundred stadia distant from Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: But when the Jews who were settled there bore witness to the goodwill that the people of Scythopolis had shown toward them, and their gentle treatment in the times of misfortune,
verses.12:31: they gave thanks, and further urged them to be favorably disposed toward their nation in the time to come; and they came to Jerusalem, as the Feast of Weeks was close at hand.
verses.12:32: And after the feast called Pentecost, they marched against Gorgias, the governor of Idumea.
verses.12:33: And he came out with three thousand foot soldiers and four hundred horsemen.
verses.12:34: And when they drew up in battle array, it came to pass that a few of the Jews fell.
verses.12:35: Now a certain Dositheus, one of Bacenor's men, a horseman and a mighty man, laid hold of Gorgias, and seizing him by his cloak, dragged him along vigorously; and while he desired to take the accursed man alive, one of the Thracian horsemen bore down upon him and struck off his shoulder, so Gorgias escaped to Marisa.
verses.12:36: And when those with Esdris had fought for a long time and were exhausted, Judas called upon the Lord to appear as their ally and to appear as the leader of the battle;
verses.12:37: and raising the battle cry with hymns in his ancestral language, he rushed unexpectedly upon those with Gorgias and put them to rout.
verses.12:38: Then Judas gathered his army and came to the city of Adullam; and as the seventh day was approaching, they purified themselves according to the custom, and kept the Sabbath there.
verses.12:39: On the next day, as by that time it had become necessary, those with Judas came to take up the bodies of those who had fallen and to lay them to rest with their kinsmen in the tombs of their fathers.
verses.12:40: And under the tunics of each of the dead they found consecrated tokens of the idols of Jamnia, which the law forbids the Jews to have; and it became clear to all that for this cause these men had fallen.
verses.12:41: Therefore all blessed the judgments of the Lord, the righteous Judge, who makes the hidden things manifest,
verses.12:42: and turned to supplication, praying that the sin that had been committed might be completely blotted out; and the noble Judas exhorted the multitude to keep themselves free from sin, since they had seen with their own eyes what had happened because of the sin of those who had fallen.
verses.12:43: And having made a collection man by man to the amount of two thousand drachmas of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, acting very rightly and honorably, taking thought for the resurrection.
verses.12:44: For if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead.
